questions.q: What problem does gradient accumulation primarily solve?
options: Slow data loading from disk
Simulating a larger effective batch size when GPU memory can't fit it directly
Numerical overflow in FP16 training
Reducing the number of epochs needed to converge
questions.explain: Gradient accumulation spreads one 'effective' large batch across several smaller forward/backward passes, letting you train as if you had a bigger batch without needing the memory to hold it all at once.

questions.q: Why does gradient accumulation work mechanically — what PyTorch behavior makes it possible?
options: optimizer.step() automatically averages gradients across calls
backward() adds new gradients into .grad rather than replacing them, so gradients from successive micro-batches sum together
DataLoader automatically batches multiple iterations together
loss.backward() can only be called once per epoch
questions.explain: Each call to backward() accumulates into .grad by addition. As long as you don't call zero_grad() between micro-batches, several backward() calls build up a combined gradient before one optimizer.step().

questions.q: In an accumulation loop with accum_steps = 4, what happens if you forget to divide the loss by accum_steps before calling backward()?
options: Nothing changes — PyTorch divides automatically
Training raises a RuntimeError
The accumulated gradient ends up about 4x larger than intended, acting like a 4x larger learning rate
The model's forward pass produces incorrect outputs
questions.explain: backward() accumulates sums, not averages. Without dividing by accum_steps first, the summed gradient is accum_steps times too large, silently behaving as if the learning rate were multiplied by accum_steps.

questions.q: In the standard gradient accumulation loop, where should optimizer.step() and optimizer.zero_grad() be called?
options: After every single micro-batch, same as normal training
Only once, after the very last micro-batch of the entire training run
Only every accum_steps micro-batches, inside a conditional check on the iteration count
Before the forward pass on each micro-batch
questions.explain: Gradients from backward() keep accumulating across micro-batches. optimizer.step() and zero_grad() should only run once an effective batch's worth of micro-batches have accumulated, typically guarded by (i + 1) % accum_steps == 0.

questions.q: Why is a model using gradient accumulation with BatchNorm layers not perfectly numerically identical to the same model trained with one real large batch?
options: Gradient accumulation disables BatchNorm entirely
BatchNorm's running statistics are computed per micro-batch as it passes through, not pooled retroactively across all accumulated micro-batches
BatchNorm requires FP16 and breaks under gradient accumulation
Accumulated gradients are not compatible with BatchNorm's backward pass
questions.explain: BatchNorm computes its batch statistics from whatever micro-batch is currently passing through the layer. Accumulation correctly sums gradients, but it does not retroactively combine BatchNorm statistics the way one real large batch would.
